comment: One row for each rule of the raw-storage producer (src/fort/ownership_source_raw.ft), the
raw report rendering (src/fort/ownership_report.ft) and the shared witness walk
(src/fort/ownership_source_local.ft) that the raw increment adds or depends on.
A row names the line that holds the rule and the text that breaks it.
The build compiles working-tree HEAD with the mutant; the md5 guard reads the product
compiler build/Linux/debug/fort. The raw module tests compile src/fort with the mutant too.
The stages run the raw module tests, the raw report test and the witness walk test, then
the ownership driver test. Run it in the Linux VM with the debug preset.
The first row of a run can read stale when the guest sees the old file time; a runner that
sleeps 20 s before each guest command (`sleep 20; exec tools/vm run "$@"`) avoids it.
The stage logs, not the `tests` field, name the catching test: the runner parses only
ctest names, and these stages run test/lang/run_tests.py.
The guards for a region without a size (select, offset_plus, the unsized test in decide,
the residue form of the alignment test) have no row: since the checker refuses an array
above TYPE_MAX_SIZE behind a reference (b172e3e9), no test can reach them, and each of
their 9 former rows survived the raw tests there.
